doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

chapter: De De's career and trumpet players
title: Brass bands and the Jefferson City Buzzards at Mardi Gras
summary: De De led the Jefferson City Buzzards for over fifteen years at Mardi Gras and otherwise mixed in as a hire for club parades.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever play much in the brass bands on the street?
Oh, the buzzers for about 15 years, Jefferson City buzzers, they still organ like that. Yes, on the Mardi Gras. Every year, yeah. We saw them this year.
I had that job regular. I was leader of the orchestra at the time.
They had the Young Tuxedo band, I believe, and they had two bands this year.
They had two, yeah, yeah. As long as I understand they had a white band in one year. This year, didn't they?
No, two colored bands in last year too, two colored bands. I forget who they used before. I know they generally used two, you know.
Yeah, only colored bands that I remember.
They began to do that years back, you know. They used to, but I mean in other words I led the first band all the time. I stayed with them about better than 15 years. Regular.
Did you play many other parades or just mostly around carnival?

Well different clubs, you know, the regular street clubs, you know, and they'd parade. I played something. They'd make up and here or so they'd break up and hire another band and all that different. I mean I played in so many different bands and spots, you know.
Did you usually have your own brass band or some other people? No.
I'd mix in with the rest of them. Most of the time I'd mix them.
I noticed Billy here has some more pictures to show us I guess. Yeah, so most spots I played in.
I was mostly for hire like, you know, and anytime I needed an extra man, I was always in the first place, you know, once a time. Yeah.
